title: Rome's third text: 2 Thess 2 — hold traditions by word or by letter
source_text: XV. Tertium argumentum pro traditionibus Pontificii sumunt ex illis Pauli verbis quae habentur cap. 2. posterioris ad Thessalonicenses, Itaque, fratres, state & tenete traditiones quas didicistis, sive per sermonem, sive per epistolam nostram. Nam, inquiunt, Paulus ibi traditiones quasdam opponit doctrinae scriptae, & duo proponit genera documentorum quae Thessalonicenses ab ipso acceperant, alia, scilicet, quae scripto consignaverat & epistolis suis inseruerat, alia vero quae viva tantum voce ipsis commendaverat. Et tamen utraque vult pariter teneri.
pass_a_gloss: The Pontificians take a third argument for traditions from those words of Paul which are in the second chapter of the second epistle to the Thessalonians, Therefore, brothers, stand and hold the traditions which you learned, whether by word, or by our epistle. For, they say, Paul there opposes certain traditions to written doctrine, and proposes two kinds of documents which the Thessalonians had received from him, some, namely, which he had consigned in writing and inserted in his epistles, but others which he had committed to them only by living voice. And yet he wants both to be held equally.
pass_b_english: Third Rome text: 2 Thess 2 — stand and hold the traditions, by word or by letter.
They hear two equal bins: written epistles and oral-only deposits.
Both, they say, must be held alike.
So unwritten apostolic tradition stands beside Scripture.

lemmas.latin: sive per sermonem, sive per epistolam
lemmas.gloss: whether by word, or by epistle

choices.english: opposes certain traditions to written doctrine
choices.why: States Rome's reading before the reply in XVI.
rejected: tradition here means only post-apostolic custom
